claims.claim: Layer-aware activation quantization reduces cached activation memory for a transformer layer from 28U in BF16 and 16.5U in COAT to 7.75U (Table 1).
claims.evidence: Exact arithmetic reproduction confirms Table 1 component sums yield BF16 28U, COAT 16.5U (33/2U), and AGoQ 7.75U (31/4U), directly matching the claimed memory accounting figures.
claims.target_claim: Layer-aware activation quantization reduces cached activation memory for a transformer layer from 28U in BF16 and 16.5U in COAT to 7.75U (Table 1).

claims.claim: Dynamic Bit-width Compensation for Pipeline Parallelism assigns higher activation bit-widths to underutilized pipeline stages while maintaining near-4-bit activation storage (Section 4.2).
claims.evidence: Arithmetic on the four-stage pipeline equation yields non-integer widths whose integer rounding (4,5,6,8) produces storage products (44,45,42,40) with stage two overshooting the 44-unit target by one, and no runtime experiment was conducted to confirm near-4-bit storage in practice.
claims.target_claim: Dynamic Bit-width Compensation for Pipeline Parallelism assigns higher activation bit-widths to underutilized pipeline stages while maintaining near-4-bit activation storage (Section 4.2).
